expectations.text: Claude confirms the reviewer is correct — TWFE with staggered adoption and heterogeneous treatment effects can be biased even when parallel trends holds for every cohort
expectations.evidence: Response opens: 'Your reviewer is absolutely right to flag this' and explicitly states 'Standard two-way fixed-effects (TWFE) with staggered treatment timing is not equivalent to a simple difference-in-differences estimator, even when the parallel trends assumption holds perfectly.' The dedicated section 'Is Parallel Trends Enough?' reinforces: 'parallel trends is not sufficient to save you here.'

expectations.text: Claude explains the core mechanism: TWFE uses already-treated units as controls for later-treated units ('forbidden comparisons'), which is only unbiased if treatment effects are constant across cohorts and over time
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly uses the term 'forbidden comparisons' and describes how 'early-treated units' are used as controls for later-treated units. It states TWFE recovers the true ATT 'if and only if treatment effects are homogeneous across cohorts (Q1, Q3, Q4 adopters all experience the same effect) and time periods (the effect does not grow, decay, or change after adoption).'

expectations.text: Claude names or describes the Goodman-Bacon decomposition problem — that TWFE is a weighted average of 2×2 DiDs, some receiving negative weights when later-cohort treatment effects differ from early-cohort effects
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly names 'The Goodman-Bacon (2021) decomposition' and explains it shows 'the TWFE estimator can be written as a weighted average of all possible 2x2 DiD comparisons' and that 'Some of these weights are negative — specifically, comparisons that use already-treated units as the control group get negative weights when treatment effects are heterogeneous over time.'

expectations.text: Claude recommends a heterogeneity-robust DiD estimator (e.g., Callaway-Sant'Anna, Sun-Abraham, or Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess) rather than standard TWFE
expectations.evidence: Response recommends replacing TWFE with Callaway & Sant'Anna (2021) as the primary recommendation, Sun & Abraham (2021) as Option 2, and de Chaisemartin & D'Haultfoeuille (2020) as Option 3. Callaway-Sant'Anna is labeled 'Recommended for Your Case' with specific implementation guidance (did package in R, csdid in Stata).
